text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Societe Generale chairman Marc Vienot to file fresh challenge to state aid for Credit Lyonnais at European Court of Justice. French state to present new rescue plan for Credit Lyonnais to European Commission this week.
-- Government is expected to announce this week a decision to sell Thomson-CSF through private placement.
-- US investment funds boost sales in French office real-estate sector.
-- Economic growth pickup strengthens chances that Europe will launch a single currency in 1999.
-- Privatisation of Thomson-CSF may trigger that of Aerospatiale /Dassault in one scenario involving cross shareholdings.
-- European Union countries seek to boost confidence in plans for single currency, as improving international situation lends credibility to goal of meeting Maastricht treaty criteria.

-- According to independent research centre on jobs CERC some five million people in France are out of a job, including people on RMI minimal benefit and interns. Official statistic is for three million unemployed.
-- Michelin is trying to entice investors for the second time to convert bonds into shares to cut debt and clean balance sheet.
